newsitem.title: USA: EPA bars sale of pesticidal kitchen cutting board.
newsitem.headline: EPA bars sale of pesticidal kitchen cutting board.

text.p: The Environmental Protection Agency Tuesday said it ordered Joyce Chen Inc of Massachusetts to stop selling a dozen kitchen cutting board products that the company claimed killed infectious bacteria.

The company sold cutting boards treated with a pesticide that kills odour-causing bacteria, but the product had not been proven to eradicate organisms like salmonella and E. coli, which cause food-poisoning, EPA said.
"We will not allow the public's health to be jeopardised by potentially false claims," EPA assistant administrator Steve Herman said in a statement.
"Before a company can legally claim a product protects people from disease-causing germs it must first prove it is safe and effective for consumer use," he added.

EPA registers all pesticides and pesticide products, but the Joyce Chen products were not registered. The agency said that cooks could continue to use the cutting boards, but said to wash the boards in soap and hot water after each use to protect against the potential spread of germs.
EPA said it had earlier issued orders barring the sale of 3M's O-Cel-O sponges and a range of household products made by Ecko which made health protection claims.
